vt_g_alias_wall.blurb: A small cliff in the Bolton area of northern Vermont, tucked in the woods downhill and north of the main Upper West cliffs. Eleven routes mix trad and bolted lines, with a fair number of moderate leads: a handful in the 5.7 to 5.9 range and the bulk at 5.10. The trad lines include hand cracks and an offwidth, while the sport lines are on the steeper faces. It is a quiet spot suited to a morning of mid-grade leading with a modest rack and some quickdraws, and a good add-on if you are already climbing at Upper West.

vt_tunnel_boulder.blurb: A single large boulder in the Bolton area of northern Vermont, set beside the lower stretch of Bolton Notch Road, where it is the best block in its little cluster. Eleven problems cover a wide spread, from an easy V1 up to V10, with a few moderate lines around V4 and a good number of hard ones in the V6 to V10 range. A short scramble up the bank on the left gets you to its base. Expect a compact, steep-ish session aimed at stronger boulderers, with a couple of warm-up problems to get going.

vt_trailside_boulders.blurb: A cluster of boulders beside the path at Abbey Pond in central Vermont, close to Middlebury. Eleven problems run from V1 to V12, with a few friendly lines, a middle stretch around V3 to V4, and a handful of hard problems for strong climbers, including some steep ones. The rock quality is well regarded. The surrounding Abbey Pond area leans shady, damp and buggy, so pick a cool, dry day, and bring a couple of pads for the uneven ground.
vt_trailside_boulders.approach: A short walk up the trail from the trailhead lot; the boulders sit right off the left side of the path.

vt_stowed_boulder.blurb: One big boulder on the hillside above the ENT boulders at Smugglers' Notch, Vermont, reached by a short climb up the slope from a neighbouring block. Its eleven problems start at V1 and top out at V6, though most sit between V2 and V3, which makes it a friendly place for climbers working through the middle grades. The long east side overhangs, and a few harder lines at V5 and V6 give stronger climbers something to work on.

vt_gem_the.blurb: A large, well-regarded granite block in the woods near Kettle Pond in Groton, Vermont, reached through the campground area and a short bushwhack. Eleven problems range from V1 to V11. Most are easy to moderate, with a cluster of V2s and a few V6s, and one very hard line at the top. The surrounding forest holds many granite boulders of various sizes, so it combines well with a day of exploring nearby blocks.

vt_roadside_boulder.blurb: A granite boulder in the mixed woods of Groton State Forest in central Vermont, close to the Kettle Pond day-use area and within sight of the pavement. The eleven problems cover a very wide range, from a V0 warm-up through plenty of easy lines at V1 and V2, up to a couple of V12 testpieces. That makes it a good stop for a mixed group: beginners can find starter problems while the hardest climbers have serious projects. A short walk from the lot is all it takes.

vt_fissure_boulder.blurb: A long, shard-shaped boulder in a hillside hollow at the top of Smugglers' Notch, Vermont, among the blocks that came down in the 2020 rockfall. It has a handful of powerful overhanging problems and some jug hauls, plus technical slabs on the side facing the road. Eleven problems run from V1 to V7, with most at V1 to V2, so it works well for newer boulderers, and a few harder lines offer a challenge at V5 to V7. You reach it by heading downhill past a neighbouring boulder.

wa_main_wall_9.blurb: The biggest cliff band at China Bend in northeast Washington, hard to miss from the base of the hill. Nearly all twelve routes are bolted and graded 5.11 or 5.12, with just one trad line, so this is a wall for strong leaders; there is nothing easier here. Most routes face southeast and pick up some shade later in the day, which makes it best in early spring and late fall. A short, steep, cairned path from the small lot leads to the base.

wa_eagle_feather_buttress.blurb: A small slabby crag in the Icicle Creek area near Leavenworth, Washington, perched between Alphabet Rock below and Wart Wall above. Twelve routes, mostly trad with two bolted lines, span about 5.6 to 5.10. The grades are moderate, with a good number of 5.7 to 5.9 leads, so it suits climbers building up trad experience as well as those wanting an easy extra stop on a day in the canyon. Expect friendly, low-angle climbing rather than anything steep.

_conflicts.wa_main_wall_9: Stored rock is phyllite, but the China Bend page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/106797978) describes the cliff as sandy limestone; the Main Wall page gives no rock.
